scene_translation: The inside of the shop was dim, and the smell of books stacked up to the ceiling hit your nose. Behind the counter sat an older woman wearing glasses, and the moment you walked in, she narrowed her eyes. "Welcome… what an unusual guest. It was テスト-san, wasn't it?" You stopped in your tracks — this was someone who had no way of knowing your name. Deep in the back of the shelves, you could see a single book wrapped in blue cloth.
grammar_note: 【〜なり】meaning 'the moment / as soon as'. 「テストが入ってくるなり目を細めた」= 'The moment you walked in, she narrowed her eyes.' なり attaches to the dictionary form of a verb and expresses that the second action follows immediately. It often carries a slightly literary or formal tone, common in written narrative.

vocab.meaning: to stack up, to pile up
to narrow one's eyes (suspicion or scrutiny)

mystery_memo: A bookshop owner knows the player's name without being told — the third person to do so (after the woman in blue in Scene 2 and the old tobacco-shop keeper who reacted with fear). The blue-cloth-wrapped book on the back shelf mirrors the blue of the mystery woman's clothing — likely a direct clue. The woman's tone is polite but watching; relationship is neutral-suspicious. The locker notebook and receipt from Scene 4 may connect to this shop — the notebook was old and worn, suggesting it could have originated here.
